set.body:
Defect: Segmentation is missing -- but NARROWLY, and an earlier draft of this diagnosis was false. view.IndependentCoding(name, checksum, intervals) (voyage.scala:163-170) IS a named, checksummed, disjointness-proven interval list, and SherlockSceneCoding.load already builds one -- but on RECALL time with a bare group: Int. core.PlaybackIntervalSet.of (:869) is an ordered interval set with no identity or semantics. What is missing is precise: a segmentation on a STIMULUS axis carrying ordinals, a granularity level and an authority.

Do: Segmentation(id, work, level: GranularityLevel, authority: SegmentationAuthority, clock, segments) -- ordinal-dense, onset-sorted, 1-based. SegmentationAuthority distinguishes AuthorAnnotated(coder) / Crowd(n) / ParticipantConsensus(n) / Derived(from, by).

Tests: Cite IndependentCoding and PlaybackIntervalSet in the ADR and say why each falls short, or 'genuinely missing' fails its own cold read.

Exit: A stimulus segmentation exists as a type, and the ADR says what it adds over the two types that already come close.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S0 last bullet; S3 P3
set.title: intake P3: Segmentation on a stimulus axis (ordinals, granularity level, authority)
